children: SYDNEY--Qantas Airways plans to launch a nonstop service between Sydney and New York in 2028, cutting more than three hours from the journey.

The Australian carrier, which already flies nonstop from Australia to London, said Wednesday that it will start the first ever direct commercial passenger service between Sydney and New York in the middle of 2028.

The nearly 10,000-mile trip will take about 18 hours, compared with more than 21 hours on what is its fastest current route. That trip includes a two-hour refueling stop in Auckland, New Zealand, which is two time zones closer than Sydney to the U.S.

Qantas is betting that so-called ultra long-haul routes serviced by more fuel-efficient planes will persuade customers to pay higher ticket prices for shorter overall travel times and greater comfort on newer craft.
That should support margins and mitigate the impact of fuel-price shocks, such as the conflict-driven volatility that led to a 14% drop in profit across Qantas's last full fiscal year.
"Conquering the tyranny of distance has been part of who Qantas is," Chief Executive Vanessa Hudson said.
"Flying these distances is only worth doing if our customers arrive feeling their best."
Known as The Flying Kangaroo for the logo displayed on its tailfin and elsewhere, Qantas has already scheduled its first nonstop Sydney-to-London flight for October 2027.
That 10,600-mile trip will last up to 22 hours and looks set to surpass Singapore Airlines' 19-hour Singapore-to-New York service as the world's longest lasting direct commercial passenger flight.
Qantas already flies direct from Perth on Australia's west coast to London, a journey of some 9,000 miles.
